title: Under-five mortality rate
national_indicator_description: The under-five mortality rate describes the probability of dying between birth and the fifth birthday, based on the number of deaths before the age of 5 per 1000 live births in the reference period.
computation_definitions: Probability (expressed as a rate per 1000 live births) of a child born alive in a specified period dying before reaching the age of five, if subject to current age specific mortality rates.
computation_calculations: (Number of deaths under the age of 5 in the reference period / Total number of live births in the reference period) * 1000
other_info: Figures for the total under-5 mortality rate, as well as breakdowns by sex and urban/rural residence for 2020 and 2025, are calculated based on the 5-year period preceding the survey; breakdowns by sex and urban/rural residence for 2008, 2010, and 2015, as well as all breakdowns by province, are calculated based on the 10-year period preceding the survey. Note that breakdowns from different periods cannot be directly compared. For more details, see the linked data source. Alternative estimates of the under-five mortality rate developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) can be found on the [WHO Data Portal](https://data.who.int/indicators/i/E3CAF2B/2322814?m49=646).
comments_limitations: Figures from the Demographic and Health Survey are subject to recall error. Interviewed women may omit births and deaths or include stillbirths along with live births. Survey data may also suffer from survivor selection bias and age truncation. Mothers may misreport their children’s birth dates, current ages or ages at death, perhaps more so if the child has died. The heaping of deaths at age 12 months is especially common. Age heaping may transfer deaths across the one year boundary and lead to underestimates of infant mortality rates. Fortunately, it has little effect on under five mortality rates, which makes the under-five mortality rate a more robust estimate than the infant mortality rate when data are drawn from household surveys. For more details on limitations, see the linked data source.
target_name: By 2030, end preventable deaths of newborns and children under 5 years of age, with all countries aiming to reduce neonatal mortality to at least as low as 12 per 1,000 live births and under‐5 mortality to at least as low as 25 per 1,000 live births
indicator_definition: The probability of a child born in a specific year or period dying before reaching the age of 5 years, if subject to age specific mortality rates of that period, expressed per 1000 live births. The under-five mortality rate as defined here is, strictly speaking, not a rate (i.e. the number of deaths divided by the number of population at risk during a certain period of time) but a probability of death derived from a life table and expressed as a rate per 1000 live births.
